name: Japan
note: Japan-specific refinements over the ITU Region 3 baseline. Sources: the MIC (総務省) 周波数割当計画 (Frequency Assignment Plan, current as at 1 April 2026) domestic allocation tables and its 別表 schedules at tele.soumu.go.jp; the MIC ワイドFM policy page at soumu.go.jp/menu_seisaku/ictseisaku/housou_suishin/fm-seibi.html; the JARL band plan effective 17 July 2025 (jarl.org/Japanese/A_Shiryo/A-3_Band_Plan/bandplan20250717.pdf); the MIC 電波利用ポータル DCR 増波 page at tele.soumu.go.jp/j/others/cr/dcr_zouha/index.htm; and NICT for the JJY standard-frequency stations (nict.go.jp/sts/jjy.html and jjy.nict.go.jp). What makes Japan unusual: FM sound broadcasting sits at 76-99 MHz, not 87.5-108 - the base plan's FM box does NOT apply here. The band began as 76-90 MHz, gained 90-95 MHz in 2014 as ワイドFM / FM補完放送 on spectrum vacated by analogue TV channels 1-3, and was extended again to 99 MHz on 19 May 2025; assigned carriers run 76.1-98.9 MHz. Amateur allocations are narrower than Region 3 in several places: 160 m is two disjoint segments and stops at 1912.5 kHz, 80 m is six disjoint segments, 2 m ends at 146 MHz rather than 148 MHz, and 23 cm starts at 1260 MHz rather than 1240 MHz. 40 m (7000-7200 kHz), 6 m (50-54 MHz) and 70 cm (430-440 MHz) match the Region 3 baseline and are not repeated here. Mediumwave, airband and marine VHF follow the ITU plan with no Japanese deviation and are likewise not repeated. The JJY entries are given a nominal 200 Hz width so they are visible; the transmissions themselves are A1B carriers at exactly 40 kHz and 60 kHz, not bands.
